notes: Beat as planned, joined to Pennod 26 as written in parallel: tournament day 1 on the field by the walls; Cynyr knights Cai there first (urddo, planned in 20). The messenger of 20 announces the competition. Comparisons everywhere (talach, byrrach, fwy, gyflymach na cheffyl Gwalchmai, cryfaf, gryfach, lleiaf, gwaethaf, mor gryf â'i dad). Cai unhorses three knights, then rides against Gwalchmai: neither falls; the messenger names Gwalchmai first and Cai second, with the deciding bout tomorrow at ten (Pennod 26). Arth, the squire, runs all day: 'Arth yw'r yswain cyflymaf ar y cae!' Dafi, under Mali's cloak with the watch (as in 26), sneezes fire when Cai wins and singes the red-bearded lord's banner.

Ending set up for Pennod 26: at the inn by the church that night Arth polishes Cai's gold-hilted sword, puts it in the sheath and falls asleep; Cai draws it to show off ('Dyma gleddyf y marchog gorau!' — Mali: 'Yr ail orau, Cai'), puts it under the bench and eats three pies (Mali counts); late at night he finds the sheath empty, assumes Arth has it for polishing, and goes to bed. The sword stays under the bench.

Productive subset respected: Pensa A tests only -ach / -af, mwy, gwell / gorau and na + AM. llai / lleiaf, gwaeth / gwaethaf and mor … â each occur three times or more in the story and in the Gramadeg (marked darllen), but are not tested.

Delta adds byrrach / byrraf (double r), trawodd (taro), nag (na before a vowel), urddodd, and compare card stages for da, mawr, bach and drwg (design §8.3). No superlative or comparative appears before this chapter.
Recall of Pennod 24 words where the story allows: Cymraeg, cyfieithu (Mali does not need to translate the bilingual messenger), dur, carn, llafn, beth bynnag, pwy bynnag.

Running words about 1,460 (target 1,450, window 1,305–1,595). Recall warnings for the comparison words against the parallel Penodau 26–30 are for the editor pass (they will naturally recur at 28 'y cryfaf, y talaf' and 34–37 promotion points).
Speaker IDs: char-gwalchmai, char-negesydd (the messenger of 20 as herald), char-yswain-mawr (a big, slow squire), char-hen-arglwydd, char-arglwydd-coch (whose banner Dafi singes).

review_questions.question: [?] 'Mae e'n fyrrach' — byr → byrrach with double r: confirm spelling for learners.
[?] 'Arth yw'r yswain cyflymaf ar y cae!' — identification with a superlative (X yw'r … -af): natural?
[?] 'yr yswain mwyaf blinedig' — mwyaf + blinedig (periphrastic superlative) natural, or 'mwyaf blinedig' should be 'blinedicaf'?
[?] 'mae ail yn well na thrydydd' (second is better than third): natural, or 'mae bod yn ail yn well na bod yn drydydd'?
[?] 'mae e'n cysgu'n gyflymach na fi hefyd!' (Cai's joke, 'he falls asleep faster than me'): does cysgu'n gyflymach read as intended?
[?] 'urddodd e ei fab' with no 'yn farchog': enough, or 'urddodd e ei fab yn farchog'?

cover.alt: The joust on the snowy field outside Caerllion: Cai on his chestnut horse strikes a knight's shield with his lance while the crowd cheers from wooden stands under banners; Arth runs along the barrier with a spare lance.
cover.art_brief: A tournament field outside the red Roman walls of Caerllion on a bright winter day (Caerllion palette: red brick, snow, bright banners). Trampled snow on the field; a low wooden barrier down the middle; wooden stands full of lords and ladies under red, blue and white banners; tents of the camp behind. Mid-joust: Cai (15, red-blond, red cloak, round red shield with a small gold dragon, chainmail, a sword with a gold hilt in its sheath at his side) on his young chestnut horse strikes the shield of an opposing knight with a long wooden lance; the other knight tilts backwards. Along the barrier Arth (11, untidy brown hair with cowlick, oversized brown coat) runs carrying a spare lance. In the front of the crowd: Cynyr (huge golden-blond beard, brown cloak) cheering with fists raised, Elen (white veil, green dress) smiling, Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) with a wisp of smoke curling from under her cloak, Myrddin (white beard, round spectacles, tall black hat) beside her. The messenger in his dark cloak stands by the stands. No text.

grammar.nodyn_en: Comparison: add -ach (than = na, with aspirate mutation: na cheffyl) and -af: cyflym, cyflymach, cyflymaf. Long words use mwy / mwyaf: mwyaf blinedig. Irregular: da, gwell, gorau; mawr, mwy, mwyaf. To recognise for now: bach, llai, lleiaf; drwg, gwaeth, gwaethaf; mor … â (as … as).
